memory_update.text: HSTM should be promoted for deeper Layer 2 verification as the most direct public-market candidate tied to clinical placement software and healthcare workforce compliance infrastructure.
UTI is a plausible underfollowed capacity beneficiary because Concorde adds healthcare campus/lab/clinical-experience exposure to a company still often perceived as technical/automotive training.
APEI is a speculative-shadow candidate: nursing education assets are relevant, but clinical placement capacity and segment-level economics require verification before upgrading.
The node appears investable through three public-market paths: clinical placement/compliance software, physical healthcare career colleges, and employer/hospital partnership networks.

Many pure simulation-equipment vendors and clinical-placement networks are private; CAE exited healthcare simulation in 2024, so public exposure may be indirect or embedded inside education/workforce software names.

node: Clinical placement, apprenticeship administration, simulation labs, and hands-on training capacity
summary: Layer 1B expansion focused on the offline and compliance-constrained capacity layer behind online/workforce education: clinical rotations, nursing/allied-health campuses, trade-school labs, employer partnerships, and healthcare workforce credentialing/training systems. The cleanest underfollowed candidate found is HealthStream because it explicitly acquired clinical-rotation management assets. UTI and APEI provide campus/lab/clinical capacity exposure through healthcare and technical training assets. Adtalem is included as a reference/context anchor because it is a more visible healthcare-education provider with hospital partnerships and clinical rotations, but it is less of a hidden supplier than a direct demand beneficiary. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
